title: The offset planet on its carrier
description: Track the gear body and the supported axle in the front frame.
question: Drive H CW in the front view. Find P (frame spin) and H (carried-axle orbit) at the shown instant.

answer.explanation: Drive H CW. External mesh S/P (30/18 teeth) uses spins relative to carrier H. S held, P positive. S is locked to the frame. S held. 30 × (S − H) + 18 × (P − H) = 0. The requested motion is CW / CW (in listed output order).

options.label: A
options.explanation: P is CW, while this choice gives stationary. The tooth at contact is instantaneously at rest, but the entire planet gear is not.

options.label: B
options.explanation: This tuple matches the derived motions. In the carrier frame the fixed sun turns counterclockwise, so the planet turns clockwise relative to the arm. Adding the clockwise arm motion preserves clockwise spin.

options.label: C
options.explanation: H is CW, while this choice gives CCW. The axle is supported by the clockwise arm and follows its orbit.

options.label: D
options.explanation: P is CW, while this choice gives CCW. Using the external-mesh sign directly in the stationary frame reverses the predicted spin.
